name: publish-article
description: Draft, review from two angles at once, revise, get your approval, then store it — with the approval itself recorded as a decision so the choice is not re-litigated later.

audience.help: Who it is for. Drives the register, and the reviewers judge against it.

metadata.why_two_reviewers: One reviewer asked for both accuracy and readability trades one against the other inside a single answer. Two independent lenses disagree visibly, which is the useful signal.
metadata.why_gate_records_a_decision: The journal records that a gate was approved; a `kind: decision` item records WHY. Without it, a later run re-opens a settled question and the approval is invisible to it.

steering_examples.description: Write up the cold start investigation for a technical peer, then show me before it gets stored.
The accuracy reviewer is right about the second claim — cut it rather than hedging it.

config.prompt:
Write an article about {{inputs.topic}} for {{inputs.audience}}.

Grounding (cite as [n]):
{{nodes.context.output.items | fenced_sources}}

Ground every claim in the sources. Where they do not cover something, say so rather than filling the gap — an article that reads as complete while resting on nothing is worse than one with a visible hole.

Review this draft for CLARITY for {{inputs.audience}} — structure, jargon, and whether the point arrives before the reader gives up. Not accuracy; another reviewer has that.
